observations.content: User supplied 8/12 preparation context packets for a later implementation task; they are reference-only and not an implementation request.

Later implementation requirement: after per-session durable memory scoping, each observer and consolidator worker must run with its owning session's `.memory/<sessionId>/` root as cwd, not the shared project root, to isolate worker-session discovery, transient result/cost IPC, and consolidator filesystem tools. Use the runtime-resolved root, not a display name or project cwd, and ensure the directory exists before spawn even for a fresh session with no durable files; preserve worker model, prompt, environment, handoff, cancellation, and exit handling.

The supplied observational-memory plan describes a two-phase pi extension: Phase A implements parallel headless observer subprocesses, a branch-local custom-entry ledger, deterministic compaction rendering, TUI, and commands; Phase B adds a consolidator and durable per-session `.memory/<sessionId>/` files. Workers are ordinary recorded global pi sessions launched via bespoke `child_process.spawn` (`pi -e <agent-ext> -p`), rather than the subagents extension.

Plan decisions include vendoring trimmed OM ledger utilities without runtime dependency; one shared worker extension selected by `OM_WORKER`; orchestrator-assigned unique timestamp IDs; default-off persisted per-session `/om` gate; and strong development models originally listed as Claude Sonnet 4.6, though current `src/config.ts` defaults in the provided excerpts are OpenRouter `z-ai/glm-5.2`, chunkTokens 10000, and consolidateAtPoolTokens 15000.

The memory root is resolved using the immutable session-header id via `sessionManager.getSessionId()` and `sessionMemoryRoot(cwd, sessionId)`; `ensureSessionMemory` seeds a fork/clone from its parent once, excluding `.runs`, and does not reseed an existing root. `Runtime.memoryRoot` is the root used by path and IPC helpers.

Current worker launcher in `src/spawn/launch.ts` still spawns with `cwd: opts.cwd` (the project cwd), while `buildWorkerEnv` passes `OM_MEMORY_DIR` and result/cost paths under the memory root; the later task requirement specifically changes worker cwd to the owning session memory root and requires ensuring it exists first.

Worker agent roles: observer receives conversation chunk as recorded `-p` user prompt and writes result IPC; consolidator has scoped read/write/edit/ls/grep tools restricted to OM_MEMORY_DIR and edits topics/JOURNEY directly. Shared `agent/cost.ts` accumulates pi `usage.cost.total` and writes a per-run cost handoff.

Observer chunks are selected by raw-token watermark, dispatched in parallel with concurrency cap, and committed to `om.observations.recorded`; timestamps are re-derived to unique second-resolution IDs. Consolidator promotes oldest overflow, then on clean exit tombstones the handed batch intersected with still-active observations and rerenders INDEX.md.

Compaction snaps its cutoff to observation chunk boundaries, excludes observations represented in the verbatim tail, and conditionally waits for observers that could change the projection; it renders JOURNEY, memory map, and active observations. Session costs are stored as `om.cost` ledger entries and summed across all session entries so they do not roll back under `/tree`.

README describes the implemented short-term and long-term tiers, the default-off `/om` gate, commands `/om:status`, `/om:compact`, `/om:consolidate`, per-session durable files, one-time fork seeding, worker-session inspectability, and cost reporting. Tests cover compaction cutoff/wait behavior, consolidator tool scoping, cost accounting/IPC, timestamp IDs, ledger folding, and helper fixtures.
